correctness.rationale: Here smooth family means the squarefree, genus-four family, not that the normalization of a singular model is nonsmooth. At distinct cubic roots and at infinity the tame degree-five map is totally ramified; Riemann–Hurwitz gives genus four. Regularity of the four forms follows from ord∞(x,y,dx)=(-5,-3,-6) and ord at a simple branch point of (y,dx)=(1,4); character separation and the two different x-powers give independence. In the j-block, writing y^(−j)=(y^(−j))^31 f^(6j) and retaining degrees 31(k+1)−1−i yields the ordinary polynomial coefficient matrix (entrywise 31st powers of the semilinear Cartier matrix, not the latter as a polynomial over the parameter space). /workspace/replays/cartier.py independently expands the powers in an exact modular polynomial ring and verifies Disc=4Δ, both scalars, the trailing-block determinant, and det=14H²Δ¹² identically. All Frobenius twists preserve block invertibility, so the stable rank is two exactly where the two scalar blocks vanish, and four elsewhere; first Cartier rank likewise gives the stated a-numbers. On H=0, Δ=6a³ and u=b/(10a) recovers a=u² and b=10u³, proving the reduced-locus isomorphism, finite marked counts, and scaling to the geometric model. Δ=0 also has q points via its analogous cubic parametrization including 0. Independent point replay /workspace/replays/4.py uses separately checked FLINT field presentations and the Euler power criterion, not the submitted counters' enumeration of y^5. The (zero, nonzero fifth-power) counts are (1,6),(3,232),(1,5958),(3,184120); adding the unique rational infinity gives 32,1164,29792,920604. Newton identities and reciprocal symmetry recover all nine numerator coefficients. The submitted mod-7 quartic factors force any rational split into two monic integral quartics, and the absolute value of every root forces their constant terms both +961 or both −961. Comparing degrees 6 and 2 rules out −961 and gives c²=961a². Degrees 5 and 3 force either the odd coefficients to vanish or both quadratic coefficients to match; the first case has nonsquare discriminant 405, the second has nonsquare discriminant 496 or all-positive polynomial in a². Exact independent FLINT factorization also returns the polynomial irreducible. A proper base-field isogeny factor would factor it over Q. No conclusion on all rational twists or absolute simplicity follows or is claimed.

evidence: The split case p≡1 mod 5 in the (1,3,3,3) row of Li et al. allows ord⁴ and ord²⊕ss²; these are Newton types, not characteristic polynomial coefficients. Cavalieri–Pries Cor. 6.4 explicitly gives a_ν=2 and generic normalizer order 5 for M[11].
Cavalieri–Pries give α_X=a(X) for four branches and p≡1 mod d; Example 6.2 yields mass 2/5 at (p,d)=(31,5). Lin et al. establish general non-p-ordinary existence or lower bounds under hypotheses.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither doubled multiplicity at a nonordinary point nor its first and stable ranks are a new structural discovery for the moduli family. Explicit location of the zeros in the coefficient space and arithmetic of the rational representative are not contained in a list of allowable slopes, the mass, or a lower bound.

evidence: The weighted mass may count an exceptional ordinary-moduli symmetry orbit differently: normalizer orders are not globally the generic value. On the affine cubic presentation the only extra affine root-set symmetries are at a=0 or b=0, since the affine action preserving the centered roots is a scaling and can be nontrivial only if it fixes a up to weight 2 and b up to weight 3. These axes are ordinary by a direct coefficient check. Thus the mass and a-number, with the axis check, recover one geometric exceptional class; it is not counted as novel.

The prior split-case slopes do not encode the trace, the exact characteristic polynomial over F₃₁, or its irreducibility. The marked support equation and rational representative require identifying which moduli point occurs (not just how many).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior implications materially narrow the originality claim, but do not imply the two explicit arithmetic statements. Marked point counts follow from the explicit support and are a consequence, not a separate discovery.

On Δ≠0, the exceptional equation is also b²/a³=7 where defined; in familiar normalized branch coordinates it is a condition on the ratio of the centered cubic coefficients. Zeta numerator and reciprocal Frobenius polynomial are equivalent encodings of the same rational model.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: These cover the same geometric family, not a similar family with a different cover degree. A normalized branch change over an algebraic closure need not preserve arithmetic twist or zeta polynomial. The characteristic-11 analogues in Resultary are not characteristic-31 coverage.

The family, geometric Newton possibilities, nonordinary a-number and equality of multiplicity with a-number are covered by prior work. Bounded checks did not establish an earlier explicit marked Hasse equation or Frobenius calculation for this model; impossibility of such coverage is not claimed.

value.rationale: The natural one-dimensional Shimura-family locus is made explicit in a small split characteristic where it occurs at a single geometric class. The coefficient equation and an independently verified degree-eight Frobenius polynomial yield a concrete test case and a simple nonordinary Jacobian over the base field. Weighted mass and the allowable Newton slopes do not supply the rational model's point counts or simplicity. The value is the explicit finite-field arithmetic and marked description, not re-counting a known weighted mass or classifying twists.
